subject: Embeddings inference backpressure after catalog change — urgent customer escalation
messages:

Cc: acme-ops@acme.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:02:00 -0400
Subject: urgent: embeddings p95/p99 spike after catalog refresh

Hi Sofia,

We started seeing a big jump in embeddings latency at ~08:30 ET after your team’s model catalog refresh. p95 went from ~120ms to ~620ms and p99 is spiking above 1.2s. The errors are low but throughput is severely reduced and our search pipeline is backing up.

This is impacting our customer-facing search feature — we’re dropping into degraded mode. Can Redwood confirm whether the catalog update rolled out a z-quantized variant or if there's some routing change? We need an ETA for mitigation.

Attached: p95_trace_20270614.json (application/json, 24KB)

Thanks,
Maria
Senior Product Ops — Acme Corp

Sofia

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:21:47 -0400
Subject: INTERNAL: ACME p95/p99 spike after catalog sync — triage request

Neha/Marcus —
We have an active customer incident (Acme) reporting embeddings p95/p99 jumps immediately after the catalog refresh at ~08:25 ET. Key asks:
- Can you check whether their routing default switched to the new quantized "q4_00a" variant?
- Any signs of KV cache invalidation or prefix cache misses causing hot shard backpressure?
- Look at the per-model worker queues (latency, queue depth) and any change in batch sizes.

Customer trace attached; I’ve asked to preserve logs for 08:15-09:00 ET. Please prioritize and post findings in INF-8243.

Signed — Sofia

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:42:03 -0400
Subject: Re: INTERNAL: ACME p95/p99 spike after catalog sync — triage request

Quick findings: we started triage at 09:25 ET. Preliminary root-cause indicators:
- Catalog rollout pushed a new default model selector for Acme that routes to q4_00a on n1-gpu pools. That variant has a higher per-token latency under small-batch inference.
- We observed a ~45% drop in prefix cache hit-rate for the Acme tenant (hot shard) coincident with the rollout window — likely due to model variant mismatch and cache key hashing changes.
- Worker queue depth on two HotShard nodes increased; autoscale did not trigger because the selector change kept instances pinned by model variant compatibility.

Immediate mitigations we tested:
1) Toggle routing back to the previous stable variant (v1.3.2) — latency returned near baseline in controlled reroute.
2) Enable aggressive prefix/KV cache warming for Acme — reduces p95 but not p99 completions yet.

Next steps: Marcus will open a rollback of the selector for the Acme rule and I’ll coordinate cache warming. We should also consider a fast fallback policy for selector mismatches in Dedicated/Hosted hybrid accounts.

Attachments: hotshard_kv_hits.csv

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, James Park <j.park@platformclient.io>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 10:05:58 -0400
Subject: Re: urgent: embeddings p95/p99 spike after catalog refresh

Hi Maria — Marcus from Infra here.

We validated that the catalog sync introduced a new default selector for your account which favored q4_00a for lower-cost inference. In synthetic tests that selector increases throughput but at the cost of tail latency on short requests (your distribution).

Actions taken (10:00–10:05 ET):
- Rerouted Acme traffic to previous stable model variant v1.3.2.
- Warmed the KV/prefix cache for hot keys observed in your trace.

Result: p95 is back to ~140ms in our canary, p99 reduced to ~420ms. We are monitoring rolling metrics now.

Plan:
- Keep routing to v1.3.2 for the next 24h while we analyze model selector behavior and update the rollout gating to consider short-request latency distributions.
- We'll follow up with a permanent fix to the selector logic and an automatic fallback for tenants when prefix cache hit drops >30%.

ETA for full postmortem: 48 hours. For immediate SLA relief, Sofia will propose a goodwill credit.

Marcus
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: slo_report_q2.pdf (summary of recent SLOs)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@acme.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 18:27:00 -0400
Subject: Re: urgent: embeddings p95/p99 spike after catalog refresh — next steps and credits

Maria — quick update and next steps.

Thank you for your patience. Marcus and Neha confirmed the root cause (selector + cache invalidation) and we reverted your account routing to the stable variant. Monitoring shows p95/p99 trending down and throughput restored.

What we’re doing now:
- Keeping your routing pinned to v1.3.2 for 24 hours while we observe production metrics.
- Engineering will make the selector rollout gating stricter (consider short-request percentiles) and implement a fast auto-fallback when prefix cache hit-rate drops >30%.
- We will deliver a 10% service credit against Acme’s June hosted usage for the disruption; I’ll follow up with a HubSpot record and credit note today.

We’ll share a 48-hour postmortem with timeline, root cause, and change controls. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute sync tomorrow to walk through the technical details.

Thanks again for raising this quickly — we’ll keep monitoring until you sign off.

Best,
Sofia
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
